name: Ehenbichl
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village near Reutte, offering stunning views of the Ehrenberg castle landscape.
beschreibung:
Ehenbichl lies at an altitude of 860 metres in Ausserfern, directly above Reutte and only a few kilometres from the Lech. With around 850 inhabitants, the village is one of the quiet villages in the district of Reutte that have preserved their original character away from the major tourist flows.

What makes Ehenbichl special is the direct view of the Burgenwelt Ehrenberg: the medieval fortress high above the valley, Fort Claudia and above all the highline179 – at 406 metres the world's longest pedestrian suspension bridge – decisively shape the village's appearance. From Ehenbichl, the castle landscape can be reached in just a few minutes on foot. The village is an excellent starting point for hikes into the Lechtal or the Ammergauer Alpen, and cyclists also appreciate the quiet paths around the Hahnenkamm. Families find a relaxed setting here, far from the hustle and bustle of the ski areas, but with direct access to nature and history.

In culinary terms, Ehenbichl benefits from its proximity to Reutte, where regional cuisine with Kaspressknödeln and Lechtaler products is served. Anyone who wants to experience the Außerfern away from postcard views will find in Ehenbichl an honest, quiet place – perfect for all who seek peace and quiet without having to miss out on activities and excursion destinations. 🏘️
title: Ehenbichl
metaDescription: Ehenbichl in the Außerfern: Peaceful retreat along the River Lech, Naturpark Tiroler Lech, Sintwag hill, Ehrenberg Castle and highline179 suspension bridge.
text:
Overview

Ehenbichl is located at an altitude of 862 meters in the Reutte basin in Tyrol's Außerfern region, nestled directly beside the gravel banks of the River Lech. With approximately 850 residents, this peaceful village preserves an authentic rural charm away from mass transit corridors. The settlement extends west of the forested Sintwag hill, which shields the village from the bustling district capital of Reutte, and includes the riverside hamlet of Rieden. Situated within the Tiroler Lech Nature Park, Ehenbichl provides direct access to one of the last wild alpine river systems in Europe, featuring expansive riverside trails and dramatic views of the Ehrenberg castle ensemble.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to the High Middle Ages, with the village first documented in 1404 as Ehenbühel. The name refers topographically to a hill situated along the winding curve of the Lech. Until the first wooden bridge was erected at Lechaschau in 1464, Ehenbichl held great significance as the primary ferry station crossing the turbulent Lech in the Außerfern basin. For centuries administered under the historic parish of Breitenwang, it became an independent political municipality in 1833. The charming Magnus Chapel in the village center was constructed in 1680 following a solemn plague vow, dedicated to Saint Magnus. The hamlet of Rieden features the neo-Gothic Church of Saint George, completed in 1900. In contemporary history, Ehenbichl gained regional prominence in 1968 when the Reutte District Hospital was established on the sun-drenched slopes of Sintwag hill, now serving as the central healthcare facility for the entire Außerfern district.

Getting There

By automobile, travelers arriving from Germany can reach Ehenbichl entirely toll-free via motorway A7 through the Füssen border tunnel and the B179 Fernpass road, exiting at Reutte Süd/Ehenbichl. From Innsbruck, the route follows motorway A12, the Mieminger Plateau, and the B179 across the Fern Pass. Rail passengers utilize the Außerfernbahn railway linking Kempten, Reutte, and Garmisch-Partenkirchen, alighting at Reutte in Tirol station (two kilometers away) or Bad Kreckelmoos stop. VVT regional bus line 110 and municipal services connect Reutte railway station with Ehenbichl's hospital and village center in minutes. Regional bus rides are complimentary for holders of the Naturparkregion Reutte guest card.

Tips

In immediate proximity to Ehenbichl stands the fortress ensemble of Burgenwelt Ehrenberg, encompassing medieval castle ruins, Fort Claudia, and the Schlosskopf citadel. Suspended high above the valley, the highline179 pedestrian suspension bridge stretches for 406 meters at a height of 114 meters, offering thrilling aerial panoramas. Outdoor lovers can walk sections of the acclaimed Lechweg trail or stroll through riverside conservation zones teeming with native wildlife. A scenic walking loop around the wooded Sintwag hill affords superb vistas towards Mount Säuling and the surrounding mountain ridge. In winter, groomed cross-country ski trails run directly through the village, linking seamlessly into the extensive Außerfern trail network.
